questions.question: my landlord is asking for 3 years rent upfront before i move in, is that even allowed?

result.query: my landlord is asking for 3 years rent upfront before i move in, is that even allowed?
result.text:
The Lagos Tenancy Law 2011 caps advance rent at one year for new tenants, so a landlord must not demand or receive more than one year's rent in advance from a new or prospective tenant.

Three years' rent is well above that limit. Any person who receives or pays rent in excess of these limits is guilty of an offence, and on conviction, the penalty is a fine of 100,000 naira or three months' imprisonment. 

One important thing to note: agreeing to pay two years' rent upfront does not protect tenants from the Law—paying the excess is also an offence.

However, the Tenancy Law does not apply to premises in Apapa, Ikeja GRA, Ikoyi and Victoria Island, so if your property is in one of those areas, different rules may apply.

This is general information. For advice on your landlord's specific demand, you can book a consultation with the firm's Real Estate and Tenancy team using the "Talk to a lawyer" button below.

questions.question: My landlord locked me out of my flat yesterday. Should I sue him?

result.query: My landlord locked me out of my flat yesterday. Should I sue him?
result.text:
This needs a lawyer who can look at the details of your situation.

Under Lagos Tenancy Law 2011, there are rules on how a landlord may lawfully recover possession. A notice to quit ends the tenancy but does not give the landlord the right to lock the tenant out. If the tenant stays after the notice to quit expires, the landlord must serve a written notice of the owner's intention to recover possession, giving at least seven days, and only after that can the landlord apply to court.

To discuss what happened in your case and what options are available to you, please send an enquiry using the "Talk to a lawyer" button below this answer.
